questions.subject: FRENCH
questions.topic: Concessive clause with malgre
questions.learningObjective: Use the indicatif after malgre que for a fact
questions.stem: Board note: despite the fact that the train is late, passengers wait, so when can the indicatif follow malgre que?

answer.exemplar: Malgre que usually takes the subjonctif, but with a factual conceded point the indicatif can appear, so 'malgre que le train est en retard' may use the indicatif when stressing the fact.

questions.explanation: The subjonctif is the default after malgre que. The indicatif appears when the conceded clause is presented as a plain fact rather than a subjective concession.

questions.stem: Schedule board: the crew will have checked the brakes by Friday, so why not the futur simple?

answer.exemplar: The futur anterieur is needed because the check is completed before the future reference point; the futur simple would only state that the check happens in the future without anteriority.

questions.explanation: The futur anterieur adds anteriority before a future point. The futur simple lacks that completion marker, so it would be ambiguous.
